I recall a particularly challenging project where I had to optimize our ETL pipeline for a large-scale data warehouse. We were using dbt to manage our SQL transformations, and our models were growing exponentially. The full refresh strategy was taking too long and causing performance issues.

I decided to switch to incremental models, but I had to choose the right strategy. After analyzing our use case, I opted for a merge strategy. I configured our dbt models to use `incremental_strategy: merge` and `unique_key: id`. This allowed us to efficiently update only the changed records.

The challenge was to implement this without disrupting our existing pipeline. I used dbt's `pre-hook` and `post-hook` commands to handle data validation and quality checks. Specifically, I used `dbt run-operation` to execute a custom SQL script that verified data integrity before and after the merge.

The result was impressive - we reduced our ETL runtime by 40% for over 500 million daily records. The incremental models ensured that only changed data was processed, and the merge strategy eliminated duplicate records.

If you're struggling with dbt performance, I highly recommend exploring incremental models. Experiment with different strategies - full refresh, append, or merge - to find the best fit for your use case.
